handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

this_session.summary: Ideation session covering LLM inference mechanics and two agentic improvement ideas. No code was written. The session started from the test 28-35 results in the prior handoff and explored why extraction errors occur and what architectural changes could address them.

llm_mechanics_established.prefill_decode_split: The full input (prompt + PDF) is processed once in a single prefill pass that builds the KV cache. Subsequent tokens are generated by attending to the KV cache — the PDF is not re-read per token.
llm_mechanics_established.vision_tokenization: PDFs processed as images are cut into fixed-size visual patches (e.g. 16x16 or 32x32 px tiles). Small symbols like FH markers at low DPI can fall within a single patch and become indistinguishable. This is the root cause of FH/MH miscounts — not prompt ordering.
llm_mechanics_established.no_pre_priming: There is no way to 'prime before the prefill.' The prompt and PDF are processed simultaneously. Instructions about what to look for DO help by biasing attention weights, but cannot compensate for symbols that are too small to resolve at the rendered DPI.
llm_mechanics_established.provenance_does_not_fix_hallucination: ChatGPT suggested adding source_sheet/source_text provenance per extracted field. Nolan correctly identified the flaw: if Gemini hallucinated 4 FH when there are 3, asking it to also report locations gives 4 confident-looking location claims — one fabricated. Provenance makes hallucination more convincing to the downstream model, not less. Its only value is as a human debugging tool.

valid_points: Provenance per field is useful for human debugging (not for accuracy)
NEVER RETURN NULL is coercive and can push the model to invent rather than admit uncertainty — road_LF_confidence partially mitigates this but the phrasing is risky
invalid_points_for_this_architecture: 'Extract facts, let the estimating model interpret' — wrong because Claude (Stage 2) cannot see the plans. Gemini IS the only model with visual access, so having it interpret earthwork_balance is appropriate.
'Too much reasoning in one pass' — misses that the pipeline is already two-stage. The split between Gemini (visual) and Claude (rule/pricing) is intentional.
Missing quantities like water_main_lengths — already captured via coverage_pct × road_LF.
chatgpt_critique_assessment.conclusion: ChatGPT's critique targets Stage 1 (Gemini extraction prompt) almost exclusively. The majority of dollar error in tests 28-35 comes from Stage 2 rules and pricing, which ChatGPT did not analyze.

idea_1_llm_council.description: Run N instances of the extraction model in parallel on the same PDF. After each instance generates its output, a coordinator agent compares the thinking chains. Disagreement on a value (e.g. 2/3 instances say 3 FH, 1 says 4) triggers a re-examination pass focused on the disputed item.
idea_1_llm_council.key_insight: Disagreement is the signal. The coordinator does not average — it flags the dispute and asks instances to re-examine.
idea_1_llm_council.implementation_requirement: A coordinator agent that orchestrates turn-taking and injects each instance's output as context for the next pass. This is standard agentic architecture.
idea_1_llm_council.odysseus_connection: Nolan observed this pattern in Odysseus — local LLMs (Gemma) calling tools like bash/python/web search mid-thinking. The tools are not baked into model weights; they are exposed by the harness at inference time. The model can call them mid-generation and inject the result back into its context. This is the same architecture needed for the council coordinator.

idea_2_zoom_tool.description: If the extraction model reports low confidence on a symbol count and an approximate location, a Python tool crops that region of the rendered page at higher resolution and feeds the zoomed image back to the model for a second look.
idea_2_zoom_tool.spatial_awareness_note: Vision transformers encode patch position, so models do have some spatial awareness. Whether current Gemini models reliably output bounding coordinates is an open question — but the architecture supports it.
idea_2_zoom_tool.implementation: Python crop + re-render tool callable mid-inference. The model says 'uncertain about region X,Y' → tool returns a 2x zoom of that patch → model gets a second pass at just that area.
idea_2_zoom_tool.key_limitation: Requires the model to reliably output its uncertainty AND an approximate location before the tool can act. If the model is confidently wrong (as in FH hallucination), the tool is never called.

agentic_ideas.combined_usage: Ideas 1 and 2 are complementary. The council catches disagreement; the zoom tool resolves it by giving all instances a higher-resolution look at the disputed region.

error_root_cause_split.description: Critical finding for prioritizing next work. From the test 28-35 results, the estimation errors split roughly as follows:

examples: FH count wrong on 3/7 jobs ($9K-$36K per job)
Water/sewer coverage pct accuracy (feeds midpoint rule downstream)
Lot grading placeholder in every estimate, zero actuals ($6K-$80K overestimate)
Water main midpoint rule consistently overshoots ($20K-$50K per job)
Sidewalk formula over/under depending on job ($20K-$76K per job)
Ballast exclusion rule (accepts known miss, $68K-$98K per job)
Sidewalk recent-2 mean inflated by small-qty outlier ($29K on Painted Rock)
Utility trenching missing drywell trigger ($28K on Lone Fir)
Paving price variance from market premiums ($17K-$20K per job)
stage_2_rule_and_pricing_errors.fix: Edit Stage 2 system prompt rules in m3_infer.py — these are the immediate next target

error_root_cause_split.settlement_mt_example: Best illustration of the split: hit +0.1% total but had $400K+ in category-level offsetting errors. Better FH extraction fixes $36K of that. The other $364K is Stage 2 rule problems.

ordered_list.current_behavior: When plan coverage pct and formula differ >20%, takes straight midpoint. Overshoots on both Mountainside (+28%) and Painted Rock (+54%).
ordered_list.fix_direction: Weight the plan-derived value more heavily when road_LF_confidence is medium or high

ordered_list.current_behavior: road_LF × 5 × sides. Overcounts where scope is limited (Mountainside 4x over), undercounts large jobs (Settlement Mt 40% under).
ordered_list.fix_direction: Add existing-road caveat triggers; consider capping formula output against analog range
